correctness.rationale: TARGET proof of complete census fails at the p=5 gap it claims to close. Sections 1-2 verify: parity/y-odd, coprime ideals via ramified prime above 2, p=3 impossibility, even-n factor pairs (104,105),(4,15) non-powers, killer moduli for p=7..29 independently re-verified empty over all residues, and BHV reduction to p<=29 is legitimate modulo Lucas-pair check. Fatal gap: (x+s)=a^5 with 5|h=20 gives [a]=[P]^r, but writing (x+s)=eps*g^5*beta^k with integral g=u+vs and reducing to H_k(u,v)=+-1 assumes g in O. When r>t=v_5(y), g is fractional (v_P(g)=t-r<0); denominators require S-integral/Thue-Mahler H_k=+-5^e analysis, never done. Thus H_2..H_4=+-1 integral emptiness does not rule out fractional classes, and t=0/r!=0 cases are uncovered. The 'k mod 5 absorbs quotient' note does not prove integrality. Separately, the artifact claim qfbsolve(Qfb(1,0,209),5^j)=[] for j<=4 is false: 25=5^2+209*0^2 and 625=25^2+209*0^2 are solutions, confirmed by enumeration. PARI thue evidence therefore covers only the integral subcase; full uniqueness is unproved.

originality.rationale: Fused retrieval plus full-body inspection shows D=209 quintic uniqueness is not previously recorded and no broader result implies it. BMS2006 solves only D<=100; Bennett-Siksek solves only P(D)<13 (primes <=11) while 209=11*19 has P=19; CHS2021 treats S={2,11,19} including d=209 but explicitly excludes the subcase 2|k,2!|lm with 5|n, i.e. exactly x^2+209=y^n with 5|n, assuming gcd(p,h(d))=1 which fails for d=209,h=20,p=5. Tables contain no (54,5,5)/D=209 uniqueness entry. Existence example 54^2+209=5^5 does not imply uniqueness. The gap is documented and open prior to this attempt.

value.rationale: The TARGET census itself is independently valuable: a complete coprime solution list for the natural Lebesgue-Nagell equation x^2+209=y^n closing the documented 5-divisible exception left open by CHS2021. It is a motivated exact classification over a natural scope, not a textbook exercise, parameter substitution, arbitrary slice, database recomputation, or tiny gain. A future researcher could reasonably need the precise uniqueness fact (54,5,5). Value is assessed for the claimed census; the present proof gap is a correctness failure, not a value defect.

checked_sources: BMS2006 full PDF body (Bugeaud-Mignotte-Siksek, Compositio 2006): Theorem 1 scope D=1..100; full-text parameter search for 209 finds only log constant 1.209, no D=209 census.
Bennett-Siksek arXiv:2109.09128 full PDF body: Theorem 2 scope D>0 with P(D)<13 on S={2,3,5,7,11}; full-text search finds zero 209; D=209 contains prime 19 outside scope.

CHS2021 RMJ 51(2) full PDF body pp.464-470: equation x^2+2^k11^l19^m=y^p with d-list containing 209; proof assumes gcd(p,h(d))=1 and explicitly excludes 2|k,2!|lm with p=5/5|n; Tables 1-4 list Y in {3,9,55} etc. with no D=209/p=5 uniqueness entry.

Independent Python re-verification: all killer moduli have empty +-1 residue sets; G3/F-mod-5/disc=3494500 nonsquare checks hold; beta powers and H_k coefficients match; even-n pairs are exactly (4,15),(104,105); norm enumeration refutes qfbsolve emptiness (25 and 625 represented with b=0).

broader_coverage.reasoning: Each broader census or theorem expressly stops short of the submitted subcase: D=209 exceeds 100, contains prime 19 outside S<=11, and falls in the CHS-excluded 5-divisible class with h(-209)=20. Hence no stronger theorem covers the claim as a special case.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No prior theorem, corollary, table entry, or computation substantively implies non-existence of other triples for D=209.
